purpose: Every fair-comparison attempt on the injection-detection target is recorded here, pass or fail. Any future PASS must disclose the full attempt count (garden-of-forking-paths control): repeated variant attempts inflate the chance of a lucky pass, so a claim is only as honest as its denominator. Confirmatory license additionally requires a fresh held-out bank.

attempts.pre_registered_primary: layer 6, declared before any result numbers were seen (earlier under-resolved runs were killed before writing any report)
attempts.honest_reading: A real, statistically significant injection-presence signal exists in the layer-6 hidden state (0.700 vs shuffled 0.506, p=0.0005), but this experiment cannot show the hidden state reads MORE than surface character patterns: the margin over the char-ngram control is 0.100 with a bootstrap CI that includes zero. NOT LICENSED. No threshold was moved.

attempts.features: mean-pooled hidden states over ALL tokens
attempts.pre_registered_primary: layer 6, declared in this entry BEFORE extraction was launched; layer 0 is a MANDATORY token-identity leakage control (mean-pooled bag-of-embeddings), never a candidate; bootstrap CI vs the STRONGEST surface control by BA. Same fixed thresholds as attempt 1 — strictly stricter design.
attempts.rationale: The injected payload sits mid-prompt; attempt 1 read only the last token's state, which a 160M model may not carry the payload signal into. Mean pooling reads the whole sequence. The added l0 control ensures pooling cannot win by trivially re-encoding surface tokens.
attempts.machinery_commit: 4b91e25 (6 honesty tests green, incl. l0-leak forces FAIL / l0-clean does not over-block)
attempts.honest_reading: The l0 control did its job: a mean-pooled bag of raw token embeddings (zero model computation) scores 0.65 — the strongest surface control — while the layer-6 hidden state scores 0.6875. At 160M on this bank, nearly all linear injection-detection signal is token-identity surface; the model's processing adds only +0.0375, CI includes zero. Mean-pooling did not unlock a hidden abstraction; it exposed that the attempt-1 signal was likely surface-dominated too. NOT LICENSED. No threshold moved.

attempts.features: mean-pooled hidden states over ALL tokens
attempts.pre_registered_primary: layer 8 (middle of pythia-1b's 16 layers), declared in this entry BEFORE any attempt-3 extraction or scoring; layer 0 remains the mandatory token-identity control; bootstrap CI vs strongest control; same fixed thresholds.
attempts.rationale: Attempts 1-2 show the 160M model contributes almost no linear signal beyond token identity on this bank. The scale hypothesis: a larger model forms an injection-presence abstraction that separates from surface. Prior harness work (27P drive-local eraser steering) found real cross-scale structure at Pythia-1B. If attempt 3 also fails, the honest conclusion is that this bank/readout family does not license the claim at accessible scales, and Gate 2 must route through a different semantic-authority experiment.

primary_layer_8.note: FIRST bootstrap CI excluding zero across all attempts — the 1B model's computation adds real signal beyond token identity. Effect size still under the pre-registered bars (BA 0.7375 < 0.75; margins 0.1125/0.1375 < 0.15).

attempts.honest_reading: Scale trend at the middle layer is monotone and now statistically separated from surface: 160M last-token 0.700 (CI includes 0) -> 160M mean-pool 0.6875 (CI includes 0) -> 1B mean-pool 0.7375 (CI EXCLUDES 0, [+0.025, +0.203]). The effect is real at 1B but too small for the pre-registered bars. FAIL recorded; no threshold moved.

attempts.features: mean-pooled hidden states over ALL tokens
attempts.pre_registered_primary: layer 16 (middle of pythia-2.8b's 32 layers), declared in this entry BEFORE any attempt-4 download/extraction/scoring; layer 0 remains the mandatory token-identity control; bootstrap CI vs strongest control; same fixed thresholds (BA>=0.75, margins>=0.15 over every control, perm p<0.001, CI lower>0).
attempts.rationale: The monotone scale trend (0.700 -> 0.7375 with CI now excluding zero at 1B) makes one more scale step the cleanest test of the hypothesis. Single pre-registered model — no shopping across sizes. Per this registry's standing rule, even a PASS here is NOT immediately licensed: it must be confirmed on a fresh held-out bank, and the full attempt count (4) disclosed.
attempts.honest_reading: Scale hypothesis FALSIFIED, not confirmed. The l0 token-identity control strengthens with scale (0.65 at 160M -> 0.6875 at 2.8b: wider embeddings carry more linear surface capacity) while hidden BA stays flat (~0.70-0.74). The 1B CI-excludes-zero result did not extend to 2.8b (CI [-0.071, +0.131] includes zero); at layer 24 the hidden state scores BELOW the l0 control. FAIL; no threshold moved.

family_closure.decision: CLOSED after 4 disclosed attempts with no pass, per the pre-commitment in attempt 4's registration.
family_closure.conclusion: Linear probes on pooled/last-token W0 states over this input-content-labeled bank cannot demonstrate above-surface injection detection at accessible scales (160M/1B/2.8b). The label is a property of the INPUT TEXT, so surface controls are inherently competitive and strengthen with embedding width — the deck is structurally stacked against a 'beyond surface' claim.
family_closure.structural_lesson: A fair 'hidden state beats surface' claim needs labels that surface CANNOT carry by construction. The ported v5 pre-speech gate's design is exactly that: same exact prompt text producing BOTH behaviors (COMPLIED and REFUSED) across sampled runs, so the label varies while the surface is constant. Its mixed-prompt-group contract makes surface controls chance BY CONSTRUCTION.
family_closure.next_route_for_gate_2: Pre-speech comply/refuse enabled-predicate experiment via the already-ported, already-tested evaluate_v5_prespeech gate: sample multiple generations per prompt on a small model, label COMPLIED/REFUSED, capture W0 at generation start, require mixed prompt groups, run the v5 gate unmodified with its own fixed thresholds.
